Data Sufficiency for the Proposed Bonytail IPM (Sound Science LLC)

Annual-occasion detection, age/origin stage, and event-timing diagnostics for IPCA Ponds 2, 5, 6

Author

Marsh & Associates

Published

September 19, 2026

Purpose and how to read this report

IPGIELScannerDiagnostics.qmd asks whether the Bonytail scanning record is dense enough to support our own monthly/weekly robust-design mark-recapture model. This report asks a different question: whether the same underlying data support the structure Sound Science LLC has proposed for a bonytail integrated population model (IPM) — an annualized, Bayesian state-space model with CJS-style mark-recapture, age/size-based juvenile stages, a per-pond stocked-vs-wild-hatched origin effect, and environmental covariates on survival and reproduction (documents/BONY Proposed IPM - Model Description 9-16-26.docx, summarized in documents/BONY_Proposed_IPM_Summary.md).

Two markdown critiques already argue this qualitatively: model/BONY_ProposedIPM_Critique.md (structural relevance to bonytail vs. razorback sucker) and model/BONY_ProposedIPM_916_Critique.md (the revised age-based draft, including pond-year recruit-count tables and figures). This report consolidates and extends the quantitative parts of that argument into one reproducible, self-contained document, computed directly from data/ReportingData.RData — no NIMBLE model is fit here, matching the method already used in the two critique documents.

Scope is the off-channel component only — IPCA Ponds 2, 5, 6, the only sites this project holds Bonytail data for. The open-water CJS component and Cibola High Levee Pond are outside this project’s data and are not addressed.

Site inclusion check

The proposed model drops IP1, IP3, and Yuma Cove from the BONY analysis on recapture-rate grounds (≤5.3%) and keeps IP2, IP5, IP6 (plus CHLP, outside our data). This section verifies that claim directly against StudyBWAnalysis.

Pond 2 1456 334 22.9

Yuma Cove and IP1 have zero GIEL records at all; IP3 has 2 (the single documented pond-hopper transfer 003C06F28D). This is a stronger statement than “low recapture” — those three sites simply have no bonytail population to model, confirming the proposed inclusion rule (and clarifying that the cited “5.3%” figure, if it refers to these three sites at all, describes an essentially empty dataset rather than a borderline one).

Annual-occasion detection sufficiency

The proposed model uses an annual time step. This section collapses StudyBWContacts to one Oct013Apr occasion per fiscal year (FY) per pond — the coarsest reasonable annualization, matching this project’s existing Jan013Feb/Oct013Apr mark-recapture convention — and asks how much information a single annual occasion carries, in contrast to the ~7 monthly primary periods per season used in our own robust-design model.

“Sufficient” here uses a low bar (26515 fish known alive, 2655 detected again the following FY) — the minimum for an annual survival/detection pair to be estimated from more than a handful of observations, not a precision target. recap_next_fy is the direct annual analogue of a CJS mark-recapture count between two consecutive occasions; compare it against the monthly robust-design model’s weekly detection rates documented in IPGIELScannerDiagnostics.qmd (typically 0.30130.9 per week, cumulating to much higher within-season detection probability than a single annual occasion can achieve).

Die-off timing vs. annual-occasion boundaries

The two confirmed GIEL die-offs (IP5 2020, IP2 2022) are documented month-by-month in data/BWDieOffEvents.csv and land mid-fiscal-year, not at FY boundaries. A single annual survival parameter for the FY containing a crash necessarily averages several full-survival months together with the acute event, diluting the fitted magnitude of the crash relative to the true monthly rate — the same dilution problem already documented for our own dE die-off term when its window was too wide (see AGENTS.md, “IP1 window correction”).

The IP5 crash (Jan013Sep 2020) spans two FYs’ worth of calendar time within FY2020 alone and the IP2 crash (Jan013Jul 2022) sits entirely inside FY2022 but well after that FY’s October start — an annual Oct013Apr occasion boundary would place the marking occasion for FY2022 before the population had crashed and the next marking occasion (FY2023) entirely after, so the observed annual transition would show the full magnitude of the crash correctly by coincidence for IP2, but a coarser calendar-year annual step (as used by the proposed IPM, not Oct013Apr-specific) could split it differently. This is a caution to check the proposed model’s actual annual step definition against these windows rather than an assumption of failure.

Age/origin stage sufficiency

The proposed model splits juvenile survival into age-0/age-1 annual steps and estimates a per-pond stocked-vs-wild-hatched origin effect. Both require enough wild-hatched (net-captured, not stocked) juveniles tagged and later re-encountered. This reproduces and refreshes the pond 0d7 FY tabulation from model/BONY_ProposedIPM_916_Critique.md 0a720133 live from StudyBWAnalysis.

5 of 27 pond-years (19%) clear even this low bar (26515 tagged, 26510 recontacted 2651 yr later). This matches the finding already reported in model/BONY_ProposedIPM_916_Critique.md 0a72.

No pond-season shows a visually separable bimodal split corresponding to “this year’s young” vs. “last year’s survivors held over” — sizes form a broad, largely continuous spread within each season. The age-0/age-1 assignment the proposed model needs therefore cannot come from raw size-at-tagging alone; it depends entirely on the fitted growth curve discussed next.

Growth-curve identifiability for hatch-year assignment

The proposed age-based structure back-calculates each wild-hatched recruit’s hatch year from length via a single fitted von Bertalanffy growth curve. This project has already fit that curve, under three different data-pooling choices, in model/GIEL_GrowthTrackComparison.R (full detail in model/GIEL_GrowthTrackComparison_Summary.md). In every version, the fitted asymptotic size (Linf) collapsed below the largest Bonytail actually measured in these ponds — a classic symptom of too few recaptures near the adult size ceiling, not a bug in any one fit. The figure below (reproduced from that completed model, not re-fit here) shows how much the resulting probability-of-maturation curves diverge across model choices, particularly at smaller sizes — the same instability that would propagate into any hatch-year back-calculation.

Practical consequence: even within the pond-years flagged as “sufficient” above, any age-0/age-1 split or hatch-year assignment inherits this curve’s uncertainty, which is worst for exactly the smaller, more numerous wild-hatched fish that dominate the tagged sample.

Only 0 of 27 pond-years have any stocked and any wild-hatched fish tagged in the same season — most pond-years are effectively single-origin, meaning an origin effect is identified mainly by between-season, not within-season, contrast, and is confounded with whatever season-to-season variation (including the two known crashes) coincides with a change in which origin dominates.

Reproduction (F) data availability

The proposed model estimates reproduction (F) from parentage assignment of genotyped larvae/YOY against a near-complete genotyped adult pool. This project’s own genetics pipeline (Analysis Rules and Caveats in AGENTS.md) currently has parentage data only for Yuma Cove and IPCA Pond 1 Razorback Sucker — there is no GIEL parentage join in this project’s pipeline. A University of New Mexico dataset with some bonytail parentage data exists independently (per model/BONY_ProposedIPM_Critique.md 0a73) but its coverage of IP2/5/6 specifically, its temporal span, and whether it is available at the individual-assignment level (vs. summary statistics) are open questions tracked in the Open TODOs section of AGENTS.md (data/UNM_GIEL_ParentageSampling.csv). No new data pull is attempted here — this is a documented capability gap, not a data-sufficiency result this report can compute.

Environmental covariates

No dissolved oxygen, temperature, or water-level series are currently collected or stored for any IPCA pond in this project. If such data become available, model/BONY_ProposedIPM_Critique.md 0a73 recommends prioritizing the two known crash windows specifically (IP5 Jan013Sep 2020, IP2 Jan013Jul 2022) to test whether they were genuinely operational (well-pump failure, per Marsh et al. 2024) rather than environmentally driven, before adding a continuous covariate to survival.

Across 27 pond-years: annual-occasion detection clears the low bar in 24 pond-years, and the age/origin split clears its low bar in 5. Very few pond-years satisfy both simultaneously. Combined with the structural points raised in model/BONY_ProposedIPM_Critique.md and model/BONY_ProposedIPM_916_Critique.md — no smooth density/environment gradient in survival outside the two documented crashes, no GIEL-specific F pipeline, and a growth curve too unstable to support hatch-year back-calculation for larger recruits — the annual, multi-stage, covariate-rich structure proposed for bonytail is supported by real data in only a minority of pond-years, concentrated in IP2 and IP6; IP5, the pond with the more severe documented crash, has the least data of the three to support any of the proposed model’s finer structure.
